disclosure_rule_applied: Names, lengths, prefix classes and SHA-256 digests only. No credential value appears in this record or in any receipt it cites. The commit was gated by tools/scan-for-credentials.py, which refused an earlier draft.

secret_name_census.interpretation: The platform exposes both the full inventory and the injected subset by name. They match exactly, so every secret configured for this scope reaches this runtime and none is withheld. A name absent from the first list is absent from the account scope, not merely from this pod.

secret_name_census.net_position: Zero usable injected credentials. The runtime's entire working credential surface is the GitHub token described below, which arrives by a different mechanism.

correction_to_a_prior_lane.prior_claim: A prior lane recorded that there are TWO DISTINCT GitHub credentials — that the gh CLI holds a read-only App installation token while git push uses a separate injected x-access-token carrying write. The dispatch for this lane repeated it and asked for verification.
correction_to_a_prior_lane.prior_claim_source: workstreams/so02/control-plane/operating-environment/l1-cursor-baseline/CONTROL-SURFACE-ACTIVATION-PROGRAMME.json, prerequisite_reproduced_facts: 'A separate x-access-token credential in ~/.gitconfig carries contents write'.
correction_to_a_prior_lane.verification_result: The claim of two distinct credentials is FALSE. There is exactly ONE credential.

proof.gh_cli_token: read from ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml oauth_token — length 390, prefix class ghs_, sha256 25ae6b184f9886fbb4d4aa7aade5958385230a79c5f21aadf3145c0bed75d6ae
proof.git_push_token: read from the ~/.gitconfig url.<...>.insteadOf rewrite — length 390, prefix class ghs_, sha256 25ae6b184f9886fbb4d4aa7aade5958385230a79c5f21aadf3145c0bed75d6ae
proof.independent_reconfirmation: tools/scan-for-credentials.py loads credential material from both files separately for exact matching and reports the same digest for hosts.yml:github_token and .gitconfig:github_token. Two code paths, written for different purposes, agree.

correction_to_a_prior_lane.what_was_actually_right_in_the_prior_cla: Its CONCLUSION. Contents-write is real and is proven by `git push --dry-run`, and the permissions block from GET /repos IS a misleading projection. Only the premise — two credentials — was wrong.
correction_to_a_prior_lane.why_the_mistake_is_easy_to_make: The two configurations look nothing alike. One is a YAML oauth_token consumed by gh; the other is six url.insteadOf rewrite rules in ~/.gitconfig that silently prepend x-access-token:<token>@ to every github.com URL. The local remote.origin.url stores no token at all — `git remote get-url origin` only appears to contain one because the rewrite is applied on read. Two mechanisms, two apparent capability profiles, one credential.
correction_to_a_prior_lane.correct_statement: ONE GitHub App installation token, surfaced through TWO transports: the REST API via gh, and git-over-HTTPS via the insteadOf rewrite. The capability difference between them is a property of the two SERVER-SIDE surfaces, not of two different credentials.

proof_it_is_an_app_installation_token_no: GET /user returns HTTP 403 'Resource not accessible by integration'. Installation tokens have no user identity.
GET /installation/repositories returns 200. That endpoint is only available to installation tokens.
No X-OAuth-Scopes or X-Accepted-OAuth-Scopes response header is present. OAuth tokens and PATs always carry them; installation tokens carry App permissions instead, which are not exposed in headers.
Rate limit is 5000/hour, the installation-token allowance.
storage_locations: ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml — oauth_token, consumed by the gh CLI
~/.gitconfig — six url.https://x-access-token:<token>@github.com/.insteadOf rules covering the https, git@, ssh:// , git+ssh:// and :22 URL forms
the_single_credential.no_credential_helper: git config --get-all credential.helper returns nothing (exit 1). The insteadOf rewrite is the entire mechanism.
the_single_credential.not_an_environment_variable: Neither GITHUB_TOKEN nor GH_TOKEN is set. The token is not visible in the environment name census, which is why a census alone understates the runtime's credential surface.

via_git_over_https.read: PROVEN. git fetch, git ls-remote and the worktree checkout that this lane runs inside all succeeded.
via_git_over_https.write: PROVEN NON-MUTATINGLY. `git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/oew3-capability-probe-do-not-create` reports ' * [new branch]' and exits 0. Dry-run performs full authentication and ref negotiation and writes nothing.
via_git_over_https.write_proven_mutatingly: This lane's own branch cursor/oe-w3-credential-estate-696d was created on the remote and confirmed present by git ls-remote.

via_the_rest_api.inferred_app_permissions: contents: read and write; pull_requests: read; metadata: read. Issues, Actions secrets and variables, webhooks and deployments are not granted.
via_the_rest_api.note_on_pulls: GET /repos/{r}/pulls returns 200, so pull requests are readable. This lane did not test whether they are writable and had an explicit boundary against touching any pull request, so write capability there is UNTESTED, not denied.

the_misleading_projection.observed: GET /repos/asibrahim336-hash/obzio-ai-coordination-temp returns permissions {"admin":false,"maintain":false,"pull":false,"push":false,"triage":false} — every field false.
the_misleading_projection.why_it_is_wrong: That block projects a USER's role on the repository. An App installation token has no user, so every role field is necessarily false. It says nothing about the App's granted permissions.
the_misleading_projection.how_it_is_falsified_on_the_same_credenti: pull:false while the fetch that populated this working tree succeeded, and push:false while `git push --dry-run` reports a new branch would be created and this lane's branch is now on the remote. Both fields are contradicted by reproduced behaviour.
the_misleading_projection.the_correct_instrument: For an installation token, read capability empirically per endpoint, and read scope from GET /installation/repositories. Never from the permissions block.
the_misleading_projection.prior_lane_agreement: This confirms the prior lane's conclusion. Recorded here with the full falsification because a claim this counter-intuitive should not rest on a single lane's assertion.

hazard_found_in_a_standard_tool.finding: `gh auth status` prints a large literal prefix of the live installation token to stdout even WITHOUT --show-token. Roughly the first 250 characters appear; only the tail is masked with asterisks.
hazard_found_in_a_standard_tool.why_it_matters: Any receipt pipeline, CI log, transcript or debugging paste that runs `gh auth status` captures real token material. This is the single most likely accidental disclosure route in this runtime, and it comes from the most obvious command to run when checking authentication.
hazard_found_in_a_standard_tool.mitigation_applied: tools/capture-evidence.sh does not run `gh auth status` at all, and says so in the receipt it produces. Identity is established from GET /installation/repositories, and the token is characterised by digest read directly from config.

container_runtime.prior_lane_claim: A full Docker engine with BuildKit running unauthenticated on port 2375.
container_runtime.verification: CONFIRMED, with two corrections and one significant addition.
container_runtime.engine: Docker 29.1.4, API 1.52, minimum API 1.44. Components: Engine 29.1.4, containerd v2.2.1, runc 1.3.4, docker-init 0.19.0. Storage driver overlay2, cgroups v2, 8 CPUs, 47.1 GiB RAM, Debian 12 bookworm.
container_runtime.buildkit: CONFIRMED. GET /_ping returns the header Builder-Version: 2, meaning BuildKit is the default builder, and the image moby/buildkit:v0.29.0 is already present locally.
container_runtime.authentication: None. GET http://127.0.0.1:2375/_ping returns HTTP 200 with no Authorization header sent.
container_runtime.correction_1: The `docker` CLI is NOT installed — `command -v docker` finds nothing. Every interaction must go through the HTTP API on 2375. A plan that assumes `docker run` will fail immediately.
container_runtime.correction_2: The daemon is bound to 0.0.0.0:2375, not to loopback. Within a per-run disposable VM the practical exposure is limited, but an unauthenticated container runtime listening on all interfaces is worth stating plainly rather than recording as a convenience.

execution_proven.what_was_run: A container created via POST /containers/create with HostConfig.NetworkMode=none, started, waited on, its logs read, then force-removed.
execution_proven.result: start HTTP 204, exit code 0, cleanup HTTP 204. Container stdout: OEW3-CONTAINER-OK / uid=0 / kernel=Linux / NET=ISOLATED / ENVCOUNT=5.
execution_proven.why_each_line_matters: uid=0 shows full in-container privilege. NET=ISOLATED shows DNS resolution failed under NetworkMode=none, so the workload could not have reached any network service. ENVCOUNT=5 shows the container inherited five environment variables and therefore none of the runtime's credentials.

container_runtime.what_it_unlocks: This is the strongest available primitive for independent acceptance. An acceptor can replay a producer's evidence inside a container with no network and no inherited credential, which means a passing result cannot have been obtained by calling the producer, by reusing the producer's authentication, or by reaching anything outside the supplied inputs. It converts 'the producer says it passes' into 'it passes here, hermetically'. Nothing else in this runtime provides that property.
container_runtime.why_it_is_currently_unused: No lane has adopted it. The acceptance machinery to date has been document review, which is exactly the weaker form this primitive would replace.
container_runtime.concrete_first_use: Have the independent acceptor mount a produced bundle into a network-none container and recompute every manifest SHA-256 and bundle_sha256 there. A manifest that verifies under those conditions has been verified, not asserted.

browser_and_display.prior_lane_claim: Chrome 148 working headless with a live DISPLAY=:1 and VNC.
browser_and_display.chrome: Google Chrome 148.0.7778.96. `--headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --dump-dom` against a data: URL returned the expected DOM content, so it renders and serialises rather than merely launching.
browser_and_display.display: DISPLAY=:1 is live. xdpyinfo reports one screen at 1920x1200 pixels. VNC_RESOLUTION=1920x1200x24.
browser_and_display.vnc: Xtigervnc and tigervncserver are running, listening on 127.0.0.1:5901 and [::1]:5901 — loopback only, so it is not exposed off-host.
browser_and_display.what_it_unlocks: A real browser for surfaces that have no API: reading a rendered dashboard, capturing a screenshot as evidence, or completing a flow that only exists in a UI. Combined with the headed display it can drive interactions that headless mode alone cannot.
browser_and_display.what_it_does_NOT_unlock: Anything requiring the founder's authenticated session. There are no browser credentials in this runtime, so it cannot reach the Cursor or Supabase dashboards as him. It is a rendering and automation capability, not an access capability — and confusing the two would be the natural error to make here.
browser_and_display.why_it_is_currently_unused: Every surface this programme has needed so far has had an API or a CLI. It becomes valuable the moment one does not.

tooling_census.installable_on_demand: The Supabase CLI installs and runs via `npx -y supabase@latest` (2.115.0 confirmed). Absence from PATH is not absence of the route.
tooling_census.curl_capability_note: curl 8.5.0 supports -H @- (header from stdin) and -K - (config from stdin). Both are used by this lane's tools to keep credentials out of argument vectors. It does NOT support the %{errno} write-out variable, which is worth knowing before writing diagnostics that depend on it.
